simple.meaning: דִּין (dîyn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “judgement.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 7:26. Its contexts include family line, Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דִּין (H1780).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דִּין (dîyn) / H1780 is traced through Ezra 7:26, Daniel 4:34, Daniel 7:10, Daniel 7:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H1780. din דִּין noun masculine Ezra 7:26 judgement ; — absolute ׳ד Dan 4:34 = justice (of ways of God); emphatic מִנֵּהּ מִתְעֲבֵד דִּינָה Ezra 7:26 judgment be executed upon him ; דִּינָא = judges, court Dan 7:10 , 26 +? 7:22 (reading יְהִב ׳וְד [ וְשָׁלְטָנָא יְתִב ], Ew Bev Kmp Dr); ᵑ0 however = judgment was given in favour of (see Dr).

occurrences.englishText: Whoever will not do the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with all diligence, whether it is to death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.
At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever;
A fiery stream issued and came out from before him.
